questions.explanation: Answering this requires separating the position from a common parody of it. Functionalism defines mental states by their causal roles. This is the position defended by Hilary Putnam. The claim that functionalism defines mental states by their physical composition alone is a common mistake about the view, often described as "conflates functional with physical definition". A fair assessment also has to reckon with this worry: the qualifier problem. The distinction between the view and its caricature is what the question tests.
